slides.title: We began with ‘raise, but by segment’. The evidence confirmed segmenting, but cut the size, ruled out an SMB rise and downgraded onboarding

claims.claim: Initial hypothesis: raise ~12% in mid-market and enterprise, plus a smaller (5–8%) SMB rise once onboarding has brought SMB churn down.
1. Rising churn sits in an identifiable group and is not price-driven in the core base — Holds; Rising churn does not rule out a price rise outside the cohort
evidence: Non-promotion SMB churn 2.0% → 2.1%; the promotion cohort is ~4.9%. Price as exit reason in the core base: 19% → 18%

claims.claim: 2. Mid-market and enterprise accept an increase without material churn — Holds at 10%; Size at the tested +10%, not 12%
evidence: NRR 112–118%, low churn, sticky integrations. +10% tested with no significant effect; 12% untested; MM churn 0.6% → 0.8%

claims.claim: 3. SMB can absorb an increase in 2027 — Not shown; Hold SMB list prices; run a test with a breakeven go/no-go rule
evidence: Core base looks stable, but Inkwell is $9 vs $15, win rate 51% → 38%, and the upside is ~$1.25M at the 2023 response

claims.claim: 4. The increase matters for the 15% growth target — Holds (smaller); Worth doing; do not plan on $10.3M
evidence: $3.5M, not $10.3M, but it cuts the new-customer ARR needed from $4.9M to $1.5M

claims.claim: 5. Onboarding can cut SMB churn quickly (‘halve it in two quarters’) — Fails; Fund it as a ~$0.4M lever, not as the churn cure
evidence: Halving needs 1.55%, below the non-promotion level of 2.1%. The activation gap explains only ~0.8pp of the cohort's ~2.8pp excess churn

slides.title: Without the 2025 promotion cohort, SMB churn barely moved (2.0% → 2.1% a month); the cohort accounts for almost all of the rise

claims.claim: Without the 2025 promotion cohort, SMB churn barely moved (2.0% → 2.1% a month)
evidence: Monthly logo churn H1 2025 → H1 2026: SMB non-promotion 2 → 2.1; SMB promotion cohort – → 4.9; SMB all 2 → 3.1; Mid-market 0.6 → 0.8; Enterprise 0.2 → 0.2
All SMB: 5,900 × 3.1% = 183 churners / mo
Non-promotion: 3,800 × 2.1% = 80 churners / mo
Promotion cohort: 183 – 80 = 103 churners / mo
Cohort rate: 103 ÷ 2,100 ≈ 4.9% / mo

claims.claim: The cohort is 36% of SMB customers but ~56% of SMB churners
Of the 1.1pp SMB rise, ~1.0pp is the cohort's mix effect and ~0.1pp is the core base
Cross-check: exit-survey shares (52% / 18% / 34% citing price) imply the cohort is ~47% of churners. The same direction, so the conclusion holds
Mid-market rose 0.6% → 0.8%: small in absolute terms but unexplained. Diagnose before January notices

slides.title: Price complaints rose only among promotion customers, who left as their 50% discount ended; the core SMB base cites price as before

claims.claim: Price complaints rose only among promotion customers; the core SMB base cites price as before
evidence: Share citing price: All SMB churners H1 2025 19%; All SMB churners H1 2026 34%; Non-promotion churners H1 2026 18%; Promotion-cohort churners H1 2026 52%

claims.claim: A 100% price step. They paid half price for six months, then full price. Most who left did so within two months of the discount ending.
Weaker activation.
evidence: 41% sent ≥5 documents in month one, against 72% of other cohorts.

claims.claim: Smaller accounts.
evidence: $2,095 ARR each, against $4,368 for other SMB customers ($4.4M ÷ 2,100 vs $16.6M ÷ 3,800).

claims.claim: So the CFO and CEO are each half right. The core base is not churning on price. But the cohort shows that a sharp price step drives churn among customers who were never activated.

slides.title: Better onboarding can recover part of the promotion cohort, but it cannot halve SMB churn as Customer Success expects

claims.claim: Promotion-cohort monthly churn decomposed
evidence: Non-promotion SMB rate 2.1; Activation gap (41% vs 72%) +0.83; Discount-end shock and other +1.97; Promotion cohort rate 4.9

claims.claim: The ‘halve SMB churn’ claim does not hold
evidence: Halving takes SMB from 3.1% to 1.55%, below the 2.1% non-promotion level and below every SMB rate in the pack since 2023 (1.8–3.1%)
Best case, with the cohort behaving like everyone else: 2.1%, a 32% cut, not 50%
Activation explains only ~0.8pp of the cohort's 2.8pp excess churn

claims.claim: What onboarding is realistically worth: ~$0.4M ARR
evidence: Lifting cohort activation from 41% to 72% removes ~0.83pp of monthly churn: 2,100 × 0.83% × 12 ≈ 210 customers a year × $2,095 ≈ $0.4M ARR

claims.claim: Worth funding. It also protects every future SMB cohort
evidence: customers below 5 documents churn ~3× as often

claims.claim: Do not count it toward 2027 churn targets until H1 results are in

slides.title: Revenue-weighted churn is only ~1.2% a month, and the board's ‘1.4% → 2.3%’ cannot be reproduced; churn reporting needs a defined measure

claims.claim: Revenue-weighted churn is only ~1.2% a month, and the board's ‘1.4% → 2.3%’ cannot be reproduced
evidence: Board dashboard (undefined): 1.4% → 2.3%, +0.9pp, Not reproducible from segment data
Customer-weighted, all customers: 1.7% → 2.6%, +0.9pp
Customer-weighted, excluding promotion cohort: 1.6% → 1.7%, +0.1pp
ARR-weighted, all customers: 0.8% → 1.2%, +0.4pp

claims.claim: Logo churn overstates revenue risk.
evidence: SMB is 80% of customers but 24% of ARR. The segments holding 76% of ARR have NRR above 110%; company NRR is 109.3% (ARR-weighted 94% / 112% / 118%).

claims.claim: The headline mixes a one-off cohort into the trend.
evidence: Without the promotion cohort, company churn moved 0.1pp, not 0.9pp.

claims.claim: Proposed standard for board reporting: monthly logo and ARR churn by segment, with acquisition cohorts (including promotions) shown separately.

slides.title: Mid-market and enterprise, 76% of ARR, show strong signs of pricing power, with two caveats to manage

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise, 76% of ARR, show strong signs of pricing power
evidence: ARR / customers: MM $41.0M / 1,350 ($30k each); Ent $24.0M / 150 ($160k each); 76% of company ARR
Monthly logo churn H1 25 → H1 26: MM 0.6% → 0.8%; Ent 0.2% → 0.2%
NRR (TTM): MM 112%; Ent 118% — Customers are expanding, not leaving
Price test: +10% list for new sign-ups: 23.1% vs 23.6% conversion (not significant); Ent none — +10% is the evidence-backed level
Competitive exposure: Inkwell not seen in deals >200 seats; Ent Inkwell not seen
Why customers stay: Integrations and audit trail (advisory board) — Value is not about price
2027 repricing scope: MM 85% of ARR renews in 2027; Ent 40% renews; 60% of ARR capped at 7%/yr — Limits the in-year ARR effect

claims.claim: Caveat (1): the test measured new sign-ups, not renewals. Existing customers have switching costs, so they are probably less sensitive, but this is unproven; the stress case assumes SMB-level sensitivity.
Caveat (2): The MM churn rise (0.6% → 0.8%) is unexplained and must be diagnosed before renewal notices go out.

slides.title: In SMB, Inkwell has opened a large price gap and cut our win rate; a 12% rise would widen it for ~$1.25M of upside, or ~$0 if sensitivity has doubled

claims.claim: Inkwell has opened a large price gap
evidence: List price $/user/month today: Inkwell Starter 9; Palisade SMB 15; Inkwell Pro 24; Palisade Business 29. Palisade after +12%: SMB 16.8; Business 32.48
+67% → +87%: Our SMB premium over Inkwell Starter today vs after +12%

claims.claim: and cut our win rate
evidence: 51% → 38% SMB win rate where Inkwell competed, H1 2025 → H1 2026

claims.claim: a 12% rise would widen it for ~$1.25M of upside, or ~$0 if sensitivity has doubled
evidence: $1.25M: What a +12% SMB increase adds at the 2023 price response: $21.0M × (1.12 × 0.946 – 1)
~$0: Same increase if Inkwell has doubled price sensitivity: $21.0M × (1.12 × 0.892 – 1)
~290 Lost new SMB wins that would erase the $1.25M ($1.25M ÷ $4,368). SMB already loses ~2,200 customers a year to churn

claims.claim: Breakeven: a +12% rise pays only if extra churn stays below 10.7% of the base (1.12 × (1 – c) = 1), about 2× the 2023 response, before counting any lost new customers.
evidence: 2023 response: +0.5pp for 6 months + 0.1pp for 6 months = 3.6% extra customers lost in year one for +8%, i.e. 0.45pp per 1% of price.

slides.title: The CFO's ‘$10.3M’ is worth ~$5.3M of ARR (base) and ~$2.7M (stress): many contracts cannot be repriced in 2027 and some customers will leave

claims.claim: The CFO's ‘$10.3M’ is worth ~$5.3M of ARR (base) and ~$2.7M (stress)
evidence: CFO claim 12% × $86.0M = 10.32; MM ARR not renewing (15%) –0.74; Ent ARR not renewing (60%) –1.73; Ent 7% caps –0.29; Repriceable in 2027 7.57; SMB churn reaction –1.27; MM churn reaction –0.99; Base case 5.3; Extra loss in stress –2.59; Stress case 2.72

claims.claim: Net = renewing ARR × [(1 + price) × (1 – extra loss) – 1]
SMB carries 24% of gross but most of the uncertainty: $1.25M to ~$0
In-year 2027 revenue is roughly half of these figures, because renewals are spread across the year

slides.title: A segmented +10% gives up ~$1.8M of base-case ARR against the CFO plan, but removes the SMB downside and stays within the tested price level

claims.claim: Option comparison
evidence: A. No increase: ARR added 0 / 0; NRR 109%; New-customer ARR needed $4.9M; No churn risk, but leaves proven MM/Ent pricing power unused
B. CFO: +12% on every plan (Ent 7% capped): 5.3 / 2.7; NRR 115%; $0 / $2.2M; Most upside, but the SMB part ranges from $1.25M to ~$0, widens the Inkwell gap and hits the fragile cohort

C. Recommended: segmented — SMB hold; test +8%; MM +10%; Ent +10% (7% capped): 3.5 / 2.4; NRR 113%; $1.5M / $2.6M; Gives up $1.8M base vs B; tested price level; no SMB downside. SMB test can add $0.3–0.7M
D. Segmented at 12% — SMB hold; MM +12%; Ent +12% (7% capped): 4.1 / 2.7; NRR 114%; $0.9M / $2.2M; +$0.6M vs C, but 12% has never been tested and MM churn is drifting up

claims.claim: Why C over B and D: the extra ARR in B comes from the segment where churn is rising, a competitor is winning on price, and our own data cannot size the response. D's extra $0.6M rests on an untested price point.
C meets the NRR objective in both cases and needs only $1.5–2.6M of new-customer ARR.
Leadership could choose D for >200-seat accounts, where Inkwell is absent.

slides.title: With the recommended plan, reaching +15% ARR needs ~$1.5M of new-customer ARR, against $4.9M with no increase, and NRR stays well above 100%

claims.claim: With the recommended plan, reaching +15% ARR needs ~$1.5M of new-customer ARR, against $4.9M with no increase
evidence: ARR bridge: ARR today 86; Existing base at today's NRR +7.98; Price: MM/Ent +10% +3.46; New customers needed +1.46; 2027 target (+15%) 98.9
Base / Stress: Price uplift $3.5M / $2.4M; Existing-base NRR 113% / 112%; New-customer ARR needed $1.5M / $2.6M; SMB NRR (unchanged) 94% / 94%

claims.claim: NRR > 100% holds in every option and case; the binding objective is ARR growth
Each 1pp shortfall in baseline NRR adds ~$0.86M to the new-customer need
SMB NRR stays below 100%; fixing it is a retention and activation job, not a pricing one

slides.title: Four moves, sequenced so that the 2027 SMB pricing decision is made on evidence by July

claims.claim: 1. Raise MM and Ent prices +10% at renewal
evidence: +10% at each 2027 renewal (85% of MM ARR, 40% of Ent ARR). 7% where contracts cap it. Account teams may go to +5% for accounts actively evaluating a competitor; exceptions logged
Notices from Jan 2027; Lead CRO / CS
≥$2.4M ARR added by Dec 2027; MM churn ≤ 0.8%/mo; NRR ≥ 112%

claims.claim: 2. Hold SMB list prices; test +8%
evidence: Randomised +8% test on new self-serve sign-ups (Q1–Q2). Track conversion and Inkwell win rate. Promotion cohort exempt from any 2027 increase
Test Feb–May; decide June; Lead CPO / Growth
Go to +8% for SMB from July if conversion falls < 7% relative and win rate holds. Worth $0.3–0.7M

claims.claim: 3. Activate the promotion cohort and new SMB customers
evidence: Targeted onboarding for ~1,240 non-activated cohort customers (59% of 2,100); ≥5 documents in month one as the standard target for every SMB sign-up
Start Jan; review Q2; Lead CS
Cohort activation 41% → 72%; cohort churn 4.9% → ~4.1%/mo (≈ $0.4M ARR)

claims.claim: 4. Fix churn measurement
evidence: Board reporting: logo and ARR churn by segment, with cohorts (incl. promotions) shown separately; define the dashboard measure
Jan board pack; Lead CFO
One agreed definition; promotion effects visible, not blended in

claims.claim: Breakeven rules: +8% price is revenue-neutral if conversion falls 7.4% (1 – 1/1.08) and if extra churn among existing customers reaches 7.4% of the base (~2× the 2023 response).

slides.title: The recommendation holds under the main risks, and Palisade's own data can narrow the largest uncertainties before December

claims.claim: MM renewals react like new sign-ups
evidence: Assumed: 2.1% extra ARR loss per +10% (from 2024 test)
If wrong: At SMB-like sensitivity, uplift falls $3.5M → $2.4M; NRR still 112%; new-customer need rises to $2.6M
Mitigation: Analyse 2023/24 renewal outcomes; CS-led renewal calls

claims.claim: 2027 NRR equals trailing NRR (109.3%)
evidence: Assumed: SMB 94%, MM 112%, Ent 118% repeat
If wrong: Each 1pp lower = $0.86M more new-customer ARR needed
Mitigation: Pull H2 2026 NRR; it may improve as the cohort shock fades

claims.claim: New-customer ARR of ≥$1.5–2.6M
evidence: Assumed: Not in the pack
If wrong: If bookings fall short, +15% is missed in any option except B's base case
Mitigation: Reconcile with the 2027 sales plan before sign-off

claims.claim: Promotion cohort churn persists at ~4.9%/mo
evidence: Assumed: Built into SMB NRR of 94%
If wrong: Upside if it is fading: most leavers went within 2 months of discount end
Mitigation: Pull Jul–Oct 2026 cohort churn now

claims.claim: Inkwell moves above 200 seats
evidence: Assumed: Not seen in larger deals
If wrong: MM uplift and NRR at risk
Mitigation: Track competitor presence in MM renewals monthly

claims.claim: Price response is linear; caps apply pro rata
evidence: Assumed: Scaled from +8% / +10% evidence
If wrong: Above-tested prices may react non-linearly; if all renewing Ent ARR is capped, –$0.1M
Mitigation: Stay at the tested +10%; confirm cap schedule by contract

slides.title: Four decisions for the December leadership meeting, and three data checks to run first

claims.claim: 1. Approve +10% at renewal for mid-market and enterprise from January 2027 (7% where contracts cap it).
2. Reject the uniform 12%. Hold SMB list prices and approve the +8% sign-up test with the July go/no-go rule.
3. Fund targeted onboarding for the promotion cohort and new SMB customers. Plan on ~$0.4M of value, not a halving of churn.
4. Adopt a defined churn measure (segment × cohort, logo and ARR) for board reporting from January.
Before the meeting (2–3 weeks): three data checks
evidence: Promotion cohort, Jul–Oct 2026: is churn fading now the discount has ended?
Mid-market churn drivers: why did churn rise from 0.6% to 0.8%? Is it concentrated in ≤200-seat accounts where Inkwell competes?
2027 new-business plan: confirm that ≥$1.5M (base) to $2.6M (stress) of new-customer ARR is realistic, given the lower SMB win rate.

slides.title: Appendix A2: churn decomposition and activation model

claims.claim: Churn decomposition and activation model
evidence: SMB churners per month, H1 2026: 5,900 × 3.1% = 182.9
Non-promotion churners: 3,800 × 2.1% = 79.8
Promotion-cohort churners and rate: 182.9 – 79.8 = 103.1; ÷ 2,100 = 4.9% / month
Contribution to SMB rise (1.1pp): Core 3,800/5,900 × 0.1pp; cohort 2,100/5,900 × (4.9 – 2.0) = 0.06pp / 1.04pp
Survey cross-check: 52%·s + 18%·(1 – s) = 34% → s = 47% of churners (vs 56%)
Activated / non-activated churn: 0.72a + 0.28 × 3a = 2.1% → a = 1.35% / 4.04%
Cohort churn explained by activation: 0.41a + 0.59 × 3a = 2.93% (vs 4.9% actual)
Onboarding value: 2,100 × 0.83pp × 12 × $2,095 = ~210 customers, ~$0.44M
Board metric reconciliation: Customer-weighted 1.7% → 2.6%; ARR-weighted 0.8% → 1.2%; Neither matches 1.4% → 2.3%

normalized.recommendation: From January 2027, raise mid-market and enterprise prices +10% at renewal (7% where enterprise contracts cap increases). Hold SMB list prices and test +8% in H1 (randomised test on new self-serve sign-ups, go to +8% from July if conversion falls < 7% relative and win rate holds). Reject the uniform 12%. Fund targeted onboarding for the promotion cohort and new SMB customers, planning on ~$0.4M of value, not a halving of churn. Adopt a defined churn measure (segment × cohort, logo and ARR) for board reporting from January.

alternatives_considered.treatment: 0 / 0 ARR added; NRR 109%; $4.9M new-customer ARR needed. No churn risk, but leaves proven MM/Ent pricing power unused.

alternatives_considered.option: B. CFO: +12% on every plan (Ent 7% capped)
alternatives_considered.treatment: 5.3 / 2.7 ARR added; NRR 115%; $0 / $2.2M needed. Most upside, but the SMB part ranges from $1.25M to ~$0, widens the Inkwell gap and hits the fragile cohort. Rejected: the extra ARR comes from the segment where churn is rising, a competitor is winning on price, and our own data cannot size the response. 'Reject the uniform 12%.'

alternatives_considered.option: C. Recommended: segmented (SMB hold, test +8%; MM +10%; Ent +10%, 7% capped)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen. 3.5 / 2.4 ARR added; NRR 113%; $1.5M / $2.6M needed. Gives up $1.8M base vs B; tested price level; no SMB downside. SMB test can add $0.3–0.7M. Meets the NRR objective in both cases.

alternatives_considered.option: D. Segmented at 12% (SMB hold; MM/Ent +12%, 7% capped)
alternatives_considered.treatment: 4.1 / 2.7 ARR added; NRR 114%; $0.9M / $2.2M needed. +$0.6M vs C, but 12% has never been tested and MM churn is drifting up; D's extra $0.6M rests on an untested price point. Leadership could choose D for >200-seat accounts, where Inkwell is absent.

alternatives_considered.option: Initial hypothesis: ~12% in MM/Ent plus a smaller (5–8%) SMB rise once onboarding has brought SMB churn down
alternatives_considered.treatment: Evidence confirmed segmenting, but cut the size to the tested +10%, ruled out an SMB rise (hold and test), and downgraded onboarding to a ~$0.4M lever.

alternatives_considered.option: Onboarding to halve SMB churn in two quarters (Customer Success expectation)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Fails: halving needs 1.55%, below the 2.1% non-promotion level; activation explains only ~0.8pp of the cohort's ~2.8pp excess churn. Fund as a ~$0.4M lever, not as the churn cure.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: All company data in the pack is synthetic benchmark data; the Palisade briefing pack is the only evidence used.

Base and stress cases use different price-response assumptions: Base: SMB 2023 response (0.45pp extra loss per 1%); MM response from the 2024 test (2.1% relative loss per 10%); enterprise none. Stress: SMB 2× 2023, MM at the SMB 2023 rate, enterprise at the MM test rate.
Caps assumed pro rata across renewing enterprise ARR; if all renewing Ent ARR is capped, –$0.1M.
The MM price test measured new sign-ups, not renewals; existing customers are probably less sensitive, but this is unproven.
The MM churn rise (0.6% → 0.8%) is unexplained and must be diagnosed before renewal notices go out.
MM renewals react like new sign-ups (2.1% extra ARR loss per +10%); at SMB-like sensitivity, uplift falls $3.5M → $2.4M.
2027 segment NRR equals trailing-12-month NRR (SMB 94%, MM 112%, Ent 118%); each 1pp lower = $0.86M more new-customer ARR needed.
New-customer bookings are not in the briefing pack and must be checked against the 2027 sales plan; if bookings fall short, +15% is missed in any option except B's base case.
Promotion cohort churn persists at ~4.9%/mo (built into SMB NRR of 94%); upside if it is fading.
Inkwell not seen above 200 seats; if it moves there, MM uplift and NRR at risk.
Price response is assumed linear, scaled from +8% / +10% evidence; above-tested prices may react non-linearly.
Promotion-cohort rate is derived using mid-2026 counts; H1 averages are approximate.
In-year 2027 revenue is roughly half of the ARR figures, because renewals are spread across the year.
Owners are suggestions for leadership to confirm.
